defects.justification: ImageIO.read() decodes any uploaded image fully into memory with no check of declared dimensions, so a small (well under the 50MB limit) PNG declaring e.g. 50000x50000 pixels allocates gigabytes and OOM-kills the JVM; check width/height via ImageReader metadata before decoding.

If the upload stream fails mid-copy (client disconnect, disk full) Files.copy leaves a partial file at the final name; it is then listed/downloaded as if complete and blocks re-upload with 409. Write to a temp file and atomically move.

Any file type and name (e.g. .html, .svg, .jar) is accepted and later served back with a content type probed from the extension; Content-Disposition: attachment mitigates browser XSS, so this is low, but there is no allowlist, no nosniff header and no per-user quota.
